footnotes.text: 1. Regardless of individual course grades, students must maintain a minimum 3.000 cumulative GPA at the end of their first year (fall, spring, summer term). All students are reviewed annually at the end of each summer term for meeting the upperclassmen retention and graduation requirement of a 2.8 cumulative GPA.

evidence.quote: 1. Regardless of individual course grades, students must maintain a minimum 3.000 cumulative GPA at the end of their first year (fall, spring, summer term). All students are reviewed annually at the end of each summer term for meeting the upperclassmen retention and graduation requirement of a 2.8 cumulative GPA.

footnotes.text: 2. Some colleges require a minimum GPA for major courses. Courses indicated in this column are included in the major GPA for this program of study.

evidence.quote: 2. Some colleges require a minimum GPA for major courses. Courses indicated in this column are included in the major GPA for this program of study.

footnotes.text: 3. Students who do not place into MATH 122 or MATH 141 will be required to take a summer course in the summer following their first year.

evidence.quote: 3. Students who do not place into MATH 122 or MATH 141 will be required to take a summer course in the summer following their first year.

footnotes.text: 4. MGSC 290 is a progression requirement and must be taken within the first year in the Darla Moore School of Business. Either ECON 221 or 222 must be taken during the first year. Whichever remains incomplete at the end of the first year, will be taken during the third semester.

evidence.quote: 4. MGSC 290 is a progression requirement and must be taken within the first year in the Darla Moore School of Business. Either ECON 221 or 222 must be taken during the first year. Whichever remains incomplete at the end of the first year, will be taken during the third semester.

footnotes.text: 5. Students in the Darla Moore School of Business are required to demonstrate proficiency in one foreign language by a score of 2 or higher on the foreign language placement test, or credit equivalent to USC 109 and 110 courses, or credit equivalent to the USC 121 course.

evidence.quote: 5. Students in the Darla Moore School of Business are required to demonstrate proficiency in one foreign language by a score of 2 or higher on the foreign language placement test, or credit equivalent to USC 109 and 110 courses, or credit equivalent to the USC 121 course.

footnotes.text: 6. The Carolina Core provides the common core of knowledge, skill and academic experience for all Carolina undergraduate students.

footnotes.text: 7. Directed coursework may consist of courses toward a cognate, concentration, or other coursework.
